* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Scioto County in south central Ohio...

moving east at 30 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Portsmouth, Wheelersburg, New Boston, South Webster, Sciotodale,

properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

structure.

To report severe weather, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Wichita has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Kansas...

Slate Creek At Wellington affecting Cowley and Sumner Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Slate Creek at Wellington.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Flood waters cover several low lying spots
along Seneca Road between 40th and 60th Street just southeast of
Wellington. Woods Park within the city floods. Slate Creek comes to
roadway's edge at mile marker 15 on the the Kansas Turnpike.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 18.1 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 19.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 20.9 feet this evening. It will then
fall below flood stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.9
feet on 03/23/2021.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 800 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 14 at 1:15PM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY NEW FIRE STARTS
THURSDAY THROUGH SATURDAY DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY STRONG SANTA
ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds will quickly develop
on Thursday, peak Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon,
then slowly weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will
settle over the region and dry out any effects of the recent
rains. Red Flag Warnings are in effect for most of Los Angeles
and Ventura Counties Thursday through Saturday, and for interior
Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo Counties for Friday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Most valleys and coasts of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties.

* TIMING...From 6 AM Thursday to 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast to east 20 to 30 mph with gusts of 45 to 55
mph. Isolated gusts to 65 mph possible. Strongest Thursday
afternoon through Friday afternoon

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 15 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 14 at 2:52PM CDT until October 15 at 12:15PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Oklahoma...

Washita River near Clinton affecting Custer and Washita Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Washita River near Clinton.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 19.0 feet, Approximately one thousand acres of rural
lands are covered by depths up to a foot... from areas near the
mouth of Barnitz Creek... to near Clinton in Custer County... and
downstream to near the town of Cloud Chief in Washita County.
greater depths may be confined to small areas where local streams
enter the Washita River valley. Some farmsteads may be flooded or
isolated by water over local roads. Some farm levees may be
overtopped.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 18.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM CDT Wednesday was 18.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.1 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.

properties.description:

419 including the City of Clearlake, Middletown, Lower Lake,
Indian Valley Reservoir, and other areas in eastern and
southern Lake County.

possible.

* HUMIDITY...Low overnight recoveries of 30-35% will drop to 15-20%
through the morning.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 14 at 12:27PM PDT until October 15 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor tidal overflow during times of high tides,
dangerous rip currents, and elevated surf.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding of sea water is likely around high
tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with
normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is possible. The
risk for significant damage is very low. There is an increased
risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and
surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal overflow during morning high
tide of 6.4 feet.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 14 at 2:14PM CDT until October 17 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WATCH FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL AND
SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY...

.With the ongoing drought conditions, we have KBDI values well into
the 700s, with 10-hour and 100-hour fuel moisture values hovering
around 25%. Subsidence behind the front will further dry out the
already dry continental air mass, leading to a significant drop in
dew points following the front. The forecast drops RH values below
30% across central Louisiana and the interior portions of
southeast Texas. Friday through Sunday look to be concerning for
fire weather. However, Saturday appears to be the most critical
day as the dry, subsided airmass becomes fully entrenched over the
highly dried out fuels. This setup is similar to the weather
conditions that sparked the Tiger Island fire in 2023, and fires
that do spark could quickly spread out of control..

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for high winds and low relative humidity, which is
in effect from Friday morning through late Friday night.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 031 Allen, Fire
Weather Zone 032 Evangeline, Fire Weather Zone 033 St. Landry,
Fire Weather Zone 044 Lafayette, Fire Weather Zone 045 Upper
St. Martin, Fire Weather Zone 141 Northern Calcasieu, Fire
Weather Zone 142 Northern Jefferson Davis, Fire Weather Zone
143 Northern Acadia, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire Weather
Zone 201 Hardin, Fire Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper, Fire
Weather Zone 260 Northern Newton, Fire Weather Zone 261
Southern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 262 Southern Newton.

* TIMING...From Friday morning through late Friday night.

* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 35 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 87.

* LIGHTNING...

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Petersburg Borough; Western Kupreanof and Kuiu Island; Prince of Wales Island; City and Borough of Wrangell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 10:18AM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger atmospheric river is expected to move over the panhandle
beginning early Thursday morning, continuing through Friday morning.
Multiple waves moving up will bring persistent moderate to heavy rain
for much of the southern half of the panhandle. Elevated gusty winds
are expected alongside this heavier rainfall on Thursday, with the
strongest winds expected Thursday night. Prolonged periods of
moderate to heavy rain will produce significant river rises with the
potential for at least minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Central Inner Channels, Southern Inner
Channels and Southeast Gulf Coast. This includes the cities of
Petersburg, Kake, Port Alexander, Craig, Klawock, Hydaburg, Coffman
Cove, Thorne Bay, And Wrangell.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.
Isolated landslides are possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday
morning for the Central Panhandle and Prince of Wales Island area
are still expected to be around 2 to 3.5 inches, with higher rain
totals favoring southern facing mountainsides. Highest rain rates
are currently expected during the late morning through evening
timeframe on Thursday, where rates could be as high as 0.25
inches per hour.

Confidence has increased for the area seeing winds of 20 to 30
mph with gusts to 40 mph on Thursday, with potential for up to 50
mph wind gusts Thursday evening into the night. With the multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall and the elevated winds
Thursday, there is possibility for isolated landslides along
steep mountain slopes.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

All residents on or near mountain slopes should be prepared for
possible landslides.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 3:09AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W has been upgraded to Tropical Depression 29W, and is
currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 9.6N 161.2E. 29W will
continue to develop and strengthen just north of the region, and will
generally head towards the Marianas. Convergent fresh to strong
westerlies south of 29W's center are producing bands of scattered to
numerous showers capable of strong gusts and locally heavy rainfall,
across Pohnpei and their coastal waters, and Gusty winds across
Kosrae and their costal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests
rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei
through late Friday night as 29W strengthens and passes north of the
island. Gusts to 30 knots will be possible near heavier showers.
Moderate to strong winds with gusts to near-gale for Kosrae through
this afternoon as conditions start to ease there.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged.
For more information on TD 29W, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and by the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

properties.headline: High Wind Watch issued October 14 at 8:55AM MDT until October 17 at 1:00PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 40 to 50 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
possible, especially through Guadalupe Pass.

* WHERE...Guadalupe Mountains of west Texas and Southeast New Mexico.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel will be difficult, especially for high profile
vehicles like campers, vans, and tractor trailers.
properties.instruction:

strongest winds are likely to occur. Be especially careful driving in
these mountainous areas. People driving high-profile vehicles should
strongly consider postponing travel in these areas until the winds
subside.

Delay travel through Guadalupe Pass or find another route, if
possible.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 14 at 9:36AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Friday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. However, strong northeasterly winds this weekend
are forecast to lead a return to Moderate Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 6:55AM CDT until October 15 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and the Panhandle of Texas, including
the following counties, in northwest Texas, Childress, Cottle and
Motley. In the Panhandle of Texas, Hall.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms are expected today. The strongest
storms will be capable of producing very high rain rates, and
this combined with individual storms training repeatedly across
the same areas may result in flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 5:19AM CDT until October 16 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest and western Texas, including the
following areas, in southwest Texas, Central Brewster, Chinati
Mountains, Chisos Basin, Davis Mountains, Davis Mountains
Foothills, Lower Brewster County, Marfa Plateau, Pecos, Presidio
Valley and Terrell. In western Texas, Andrews, Borden, Crane,
Dawson, Ector, Gaines, Glasscock, Howard, Loving, Martin, Midland,
Mitchell, Reagan, Reeves County Plains, Scurry, Upton, Ward and
Winkler.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture from Hurricane Simon will stream over West Texas the
next several days. Periods of heavy rain are expected from this
system that will likely cause flash flooding, especially in urban
areas and low water crossings where drainage is poor.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

beaches.

currents and other hazards are possible.  Caution should be used

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 14 at 4:17PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "High" for development by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center, and is the subject of a Tropical Cyclone
Formation Alert, meaning development into a significant tropical
cyclone (a tropical depression) is expected within 24 hours. 96W is
currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 8.7N 160.7E, and
continues to develop and strengthen just north of the region.
Convergent fresh to strong westerlies south of 96W's center are
producing bands of scattered to numerous showers capable of strong
gusts and locally heavy rainfall, across Kosrae, Pohnpei, and their
adjacent coastal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests rainfall
amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei through late
Friday night as 96W strengthens and passes north of the island, with
an additional 1 to 2 inches possible for Kosrae through early
Thursday morning as conditions start to ease there. Gusts to 30 knots
will be possible near heavier showers.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged.
Keep up to date with the latest information from the National Weather
Service in Tiyan, Guam, and your local emergency management.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS THROUGH THURSDAY NIGHT AS INVEST 96W PASSES TO THE NORTH

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 13 at 2:36PM PDT until October 14 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 0.8 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 0.8 ft above normal (6.62 ft MLLW) at 1:46 PM
Wednesday 10/14. This prediction includes up to 0.9 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 PM PDT WEDNESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Jefferson; Shelby
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 13 at 2:33PM CDT by NWS Birmingham AL
properties.description:
AQABMX

The Alabama Department of Environmental Management, ADEM, has issued
an Air Quality Alert for Jefferson and Shelby Counties for
Wednesday, October 14.

Under Code Orange conditions, ground level ozone concentrations are
expected to reach levels that are unhealthy for sensitive groups.
Children and people with asthma are individuals most at risk under
these expected conditions.

ADEM recommends the following actions during an air quality alert
for ozone:

Conserve electricity and set your air conditioner at a higher
temperature.

Limit driving and combine errands.

Use the bus or car pool to work.

Avoid use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment.

Refuel cars and trucks after 6 PM.

Limit engine idling.

Use household, workshop, and garden chemicals in ways that keep
evaporation to a minimum, or try to avoid them when poor air quality
is forecast.

If breathing becomes difficult, move indoors.

For more information on what to do on an air quality alert day,
visit the Environmental Protection Agency website at airnow.gov
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: CODE ORANGE AIR QUALITY ALERT HAS BEEN ISSUED FOR JEFFERSON AND SHELBY COUNTIES

properties.areaDesc: Guam, GU; Rota, MP; Saipan, MP; Tinian, MP
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.
